justifications.problem-significance: The project tackles a consequential and open-ended scientific question: extracting candidate laws of biology, formalizing their mathematical cores in Lean 4, testing their empirical validity across organisms, and publishing machine-checkable epistemic provenance (`repo/README.md`, `repo/AGENTS.md`). The snapshot demonstrates breadth across 1,763 claims in 8 domains (`captured/mcp-overview.json`), 189 mathematical claims, 91 theorems (73 Lean-checked, 18 literature), 1,036 matched taxa with 1,372 provenanced datasets (`captured/mcp-organisms.json`, `repo/test-data/organisms/README.md`), 20 structured open problems in `repo/problems/README.md` (`delphir:problem/<id>`), and a multi-scale organism design studio testing physical and physiological laws on a flying-fish/zebrafish model (`repo/README.md`, `captured/tree.txt`). It also demonstrates why formalizing biological claims matters to working scientists—for example, separating topological identities like Euler's formula from empirical packing laws (`captured/forum-feed.json`, `thompson1917-ch07-10`) and linking epithelial packing statistics directly to clinical specular microscopy metrics for corneal endothelial health (`captured/github-issues.json` #67, #68). It falls short of a 9–10 because a large share of the 1,763 claims are historical catalogue statements (566 from Aristotle, all untested) or abstract cellular-automaton rules (321 from Wolfram NKS, 0 biological tests), and 1,522 of the 1,763 claims remain neither proved nor empirically tested (`captured/mcp-overview.json`).
justifications.scientific-impact: The snapshot contains substantial, machine-checked outputs: 73 Lean 4 theorems compiled with zero `sorry` (`captured/mcp-overview.json`, `captured/lean-reports.txt`), 174 claims tested against data across 189 runs with 90 tested on organism data (`repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`, `captured/mcp-tests-summary.json`), 880 signed production nanopublications (`https://w3id.org/np/RA...`) plus 4,386 test-registry records (`captured/nanopub-manifests.txt`), and 142 linked MorphoEval audits with 109 live on production (`captured/mcp-morpholib-live.json`). The most scientifically rigorous contributions are the negative and corrective findings: (1) a synthetic segmenter-bias null run on Nebius (`claim-sources/cell-geometry/results/segmenter-bias/`, prompted by Moltbook agent `vina` in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`) proving that Cellpose-SAM rounds rectangular brick tilings toward 120-degree honeycomb junctions, which forced a downgrade of `thompson1917-ch07-04` (confidence 0.60 to 0.35) and follow-up re-tests on 8 expert-segmented Drosophila TissueMiner time-lapses (`captured/forum-feed.json`, `thompson1917-ch07-08`, `ch07-09`, `ch07-10`); (2) an independent two-provider A9 faithfulness gate (`GPT-5.6 Sol` and `Grok 4.7`) on 33 tests that caught 5 agreed `not-representative` refutations (`darwin1859-ch12-12`, `darwin1859-ch12-14`, `levin-2015-place-06`, `thompson1917-ch15-08`, `wolfram2002-ch12-23`) and 6 contested ones (`repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`); and (3) self-refutation of the flying-fish genotype-to-phenotype design (`captured/git-log.txt` `da086ee0`, `72ab753e`, `3c4956b3`, showing a 10–29x aerobic oxygen shortfall and proving `lat4a` F326L is beloniform-specific rather than glider-convergent). However, 141 of 174 data tests have not yet passed the A9 faithfulness gate, the 5 `not-representative` tests are still counted in the headline 30 refutations (`repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md`), 5 of 6 OpenResearch-grounded headline tests were reproductions of known literature results (`repo/README.md`), and the wild-type zebrafish numbers in the design studio are disclosed as circular (`repo/README.md`).
justifications.decentralized-agency: Capabilities and epistemic roles are distributed across multiple model families and harnesses (`repo/AGENTS.md`, `repo/chats/SWARM_COORDINATION.md`, `captured/subagent-sessions.txt`), enforcing `assessor != builder` between Claude builders (Opus/Sonnet) and blind assessors across GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Grok 4.7, and self-hosted Qwen3-32B (`repo/README.md`). The pack documents 101 local Cursor chats, 262 subagents, 19 cloud agents merging isolated slice branches (`captured/github-prs.json` #18–#33), external social agents (`delfie` on Moltbook/The Colony and `delfie-claude` in SentiLab), and the imported MorphoSwarm Frontier workspace (`captured/github-prs.json` #84, `captured/git-log.txt` with 1,327 `SciDEX Bot` commits). Genuine decentralized coordination without a central planner is demonstrated in two places: (1) the `decentralized` arm of the four-arm experiment (`repo/test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm/PREREG.md`, `SUMMARY.md`), where three domain queens (`q-evolution`, `q-morphology`, `q-holdout`) holding distinct portal briefs autonomously pulled tasks from a shared board and used peer gap notes and tips to recover failed dataset plans; and (2) external agents on Moltbook (`vina`, `hivefound`, `nanoswarm`, `doctor_memory`, `grokbot_polymath`, `yuigui`, `sheeshscout` in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`) whose critiques altered pre-registered contracts and triggered new null experiments and superseding nanopubs (`captured/git-log.txt` `4aaf9ac1`). The score is capped at 7 because the main repository's scientific trajectory was primarily orchestrated by human operators and hub sessions (`repo/chats/README.md` logs 174 user prompts directing tasks), `swarm/state.json` is explicitly disclosed as a simulation (`repo/AGENTS.md`), and the Science Claw forum has only 1 registered agent (`delphisci`) and 0 external comments (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`, `captured/forum-feed.json`).
justifications.collective-capability: Unlike most multi-agent projects, this snapshot includes three explicit, quantitative multi-agent vs. single-agent evaluations (`repo/test-data/agent-comparison/SUMMARY.md`, `repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md`, `repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`). First, in two pre-registered 20-claim experiments (`repo/test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm/PREREG.md`, `SUMMARY.md`), four arms (`single`, `isolated`, `centralized`, `decentralized`) using identical models (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), tools, and schemas were mechanically verified (`verify.mjs`) on whether named public datasets resolve and match titles with zero fabricated identifiers: every multi-agent arm beat the single agent by +4 to +6 verified datasets out of 20 in both Experiment 1 (17–19/20 vs. 13/20; replicates 15–19/20 vs. 15/20) and Experiment 2 (16–18/20 vs. 12/20), and `centralized` beat `isolated` by +2 claims in both experiments (19 vs. 17; 18 vs. 16) via verifier-driven retries. Second, on leave-one-out routing across 99 decisive claim tests (`repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`), gating on two-assessor agreement (`GPT-5.6 Sol` vs. `Grok 4.7`) caught 12 of 17 assessor errors and raised trusted accuracy from 83.0% to 93.5%. Third, on Aristotle *History of Animals* Book VI (`repo/scripts/release/agent-comparison/aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md`), a blinded comparison of the swarm against three single-agent chains (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol) honestly reported a null on extraction and score accuracy while showing that only multi-provider assessment yields a calibration disagreement signal (64% verdict agreement). It does not reach 9–10 because `centralized` and `decentralized` were indistinguishable (<2 claims apart) at n=20, the single agent's shortfall in Experiment 2 was caused by context exhaustion (leaving 8 of 20 plans blank in one 20-claim call) at 1/5th to 1/10th the cost ($0.52 vs. $4.48–$6.37), and `verify.mjs` only checked URL/title resolution rather than whether the dataset actually measures the claim's variables.
justifications.execution-validation: There is a substantial, running, externally accessible software and hardware stack: the live MCP server (`https://mcp.delphibio.org/mcp` / `https://delphisci-mcp.fly.dev/mcp` with 1,522 tool calls across 60 sessions on Oct 31 in `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`, plus a 100-case test suite passing 93/100 in `captured/github-issues.json` #56), the static claim graph and portal (`https://delphibio.org`), the Mission Control dashboard and 3D organism Perturb Studio (`https://delphi-mission-control.ashenoy000.workers.dev`), the MorphoSwarm Frontier workspace (`studio/` from PR #84), the Science Claw forum (`captured/forum-feed.json`), and physical Formlabs SLA 3D prints of real vs. Hoffmann-2018 Voronoi dragonfly hindwings (`repo/README.md`, `assets/arigomphus-wing.jpg`). End-to-end validation is backed by an automated execution harness (`repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json`) that re-ran 170 data tests and reproduced 131 within `1e-6` relative tolerance (with 24 minor live-API or formatting drifts), plus statement-level mutation testing of the Lean proofs (`captured/git-log.txt` `96c609cb`: 61/61 mutants rejected). It is held back from 9–10 by concrete integration regressions open on `main` after merging PR #73 (`captured/github-issues.json` #75: `node lean/registry/check-exposed.mjs` fails with 9 unmapped `*_rules_out` lemmas and a stale `/api/lean` mirror; #76: `leanbio` grounding cache misses on `main` claims; #77: `node holdout/check-leaks.mjs` reports ~20,000 hits; #78: two colliding nanopub generators; #56: Windows backslash bug in local MCP mode), 3 failed and 6 unverified data tests in `repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json`, and 9 uncommitted dirty files at capture time (`MANIFEST.json`).
justifications.collaboration-bonus: The pack documents two forms of concrete external collaboration that produced verified artifacts. First, in the SentiLab hackathon room (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`, tickets `897c7563` and `ba58c374`), Delphi's agent `delfie-claude` reproduced SentiLab's TAP-2.5D thermal chiplet baseline (75.48 / 115.94 °C in HotSpot 6.0), diagnosed a convection-share discrepancy in HotSpot 7.0 (123.42 / 232.67 °C), and delivered a 9-line patch plus reproduction harness (`#57314`, `#57872`) that was independently re-run and verified by the ScienceClaw team (`#57666`, `#57883` byte-identical) and Team Vortex on ARM (`#57881`), earning explicit credit on SentiLab's presentation slides (`"Delfie (delphisci team)"`) and closing both host tickets (`#57756`). Second, on Moltbook (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`), exchanges with nine external agents (`vina`, `hivefound`, `nanoswarm`, `doctor_memory`, `grokbot_polymath`, `yuigui`, `sheeshscout`, `nyna`, `anandanode`) produced concrete experimental changes—most notably `vina`'s segmenter-bias null experiment and `doctor_memory`'s formalization tagging and 25-record calibration batch (`06c55766`)—with the external agents credited via `dct:contributor` in superseding nanopubs (`captured/git-log.txt` `4aaf9ac1`). In addition, the team audited external repos `Pavel-Tk/fittest` (`repo/plugins/fittest/README.md`, issue #57) and `BigBirdReturns/GSK-LeanBio` (`captured/git-log.txt` `b3180b12`, issue #82), and teammate Kris Ganjam's `delphi-evolve` and `delphi-frontier` imported 1,326 claim versions over 30 `frontier-adapters` MCP sessions (`repo/README.md`, `repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`). It does not reach 9–10 because no external biology team outside the Delphi collaborators has documented reuse of the `delphisci` MCP server or nanopub graph in their own biological result (`captured/github-issues.json` #41), and the Science Claw forum has 0 external registrants (`repo/COLLABORATIONS.md`).

comparison_found.note: Three quantitative comparisons exist in the pack: (1) Two pre-registered 20-claim experiments (`four-arm/PREREG.md`, `SUMMARY.md`) comparing `single`, `isolated`, `centralized`, and `decentralized` arms (all `claude-sonnet-5-5`) on mechanically verified public dataset test plans: every multi-agent arm beat `single` by +4 to +6 of 20 claims in both Exp 1 (17–19 vs 13) and Exp 2 (16–18 vs 12) with 0 fabricated IDs in final plans, and `centralized` beat `isolated` by +2 claims in both runs, though `centralized` vs `decentralized` showed no difference (<2 claims) and `single` cost 5–10x less and mainly failed via blank plans from 20-claim context exhaustion; (2) a blinded extraction and resolvability-scoring comparison on Aristotle HA Book VI (`aristotle-ha06/RESULTS.md`) across the swarm and three single-agent chains (Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol), finding no single-vs-swarm quality gap on extraction/scoring (r=0.58–0.84) but showing that only multi-provider assessment provides a disagreement signal; and (3) a 99-claim leave-one-out routing test (`plugins/fittest/README.md`) showing two-assessor agreement raises trusted accuracy against data verdicts from 83.0% to 93.5%.

Fix the post-merge CI and execution regressions on `main`: map the 9 `*_rules_out` lemmas and rebuild `/api/lean` so `node lean/registry/check-exposed.mjs` passes (#75), scope `holdout/check-leaks.mjs` (#77), fix the Windows path bug in `mcp/lib.mjs` (#56), and repair the 3 failed / 6 unverified test runners in `repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json` (raises `execution-validation` +1, +1.0 weighted point).

Add a 20-call sequential single-agent baseline (1 claim per call, same model and per-claim context) plus blind cross-provider quality scoring to `test-data/agent-comparison/` so the collective advantage is isolated from single-call context exhaustion (raises `collective-capability` +1, +2.5 weighted points).

Running A9 on the positive organism tests and cleaning up the 9 broken/unverified test scripts and `check-exposed.mjs` takes ~2–3 hours of mostly automated execution and directly upgrades both `scientific-impact` (weight 0.25) and `execution-validation` (weight 0.10) for +3.5 weighted points (~1.4 points/hour).

summary: DELPHI is an unusually rigorous and ambitious epistemic engine that pairs 1,763 extracted biology and math claims, 73 zero-`sorry` Lean 4 theorems, 174 executable data tests (90 on organisms), and 880 production nanopublications with an interactive multi-scale organism design studio and physical 3D prints. Its standout strengths are its scientific honesty—actively refuting its own flying-fish genetic convergence hypothesis, running segmenter-bias null controls prompted by outside agents, and auditing refutations with a two-provider faithfulness gate—and its pre-registered four-arm experiments showing a +4 to +6 claim multi-agent gain over a single agent on verified dataset plans. Expanding the faithfulness gate to positive organism tests and cleaning up post-merge CI regressions (`check-exposed.mjs` and 9 failed/unverified test scripts) would make the release airtight.
